_comment: Environment settings. Edit these values to match your domain before first use.
_sqlComment: Every SQL statement the module can run is declared here and nowhere else.
A role file refers to an action only by name, so changing a table or adding a
system is a config edit rather than a code edit.
existsQuery must return a count; if it returns > 0 the action is skipped, which
is what makes re-running a partially failed onboarding safe.
Values are always passed as SqlParameters - never concatenate into these strings.

CreateUser.description: Insert the user record into the Intranet. EmployeeNumber comes from the console prompt of the same name.
CreateUser.existsQuery: SELECT COUNT(1) FROM [edc3_intranet].[dbo].[teammate] WHERE user_id = @intranetUserId OR personnum = @EmployeeNumber
CreateUser.statement: INSERT INTO [edc3_intranet].[dbo].[teammate] (user_id, first_name, last_name, Email, personnum, change_pass, job_type, disabled) VALUES (@intranetUserId, @firstname, @lastname, @email, @EmployeeNumber, 1, 0, 0)

GrantRole.description: Assign a Intranet role. RoleCode is supplied per job function in that function's role file.
GrantRole.existsQuery: SELECT COUNT(1) FROM [edc3_intranet].[dbo].[acl_tm_role] r JOIN [edc3_intranet].[dbo].[teammate] u ON u.tm_id = r.tm_id WHERE u.personnum = @EmployeeNumber AND r.role_id = @RoleCode
GrantRole.statement: INSERT INTO [edc3_intranet].[dbo].[acl_tm_role] (tm_id, role_id) SELECT tm_id, @RoleCode FROM [edc3_intranet].[dbo].[teammate] WHERE personnum = @EmployeeNumber

CreateUser.description: Add the user to the ticketing system's user table.
CreateUser.statement: INSERT INTO [JitBitHelpDesk].[dbo].[hdUsers] (UserName, Email, FirstName, LastName, CompanyID, Disabled, Password) VALUES (@email, @email, @firstName, @lastName, @hdCompany, 0, 'Hershey1')

_parameterComment: Any @Name in a statement is filled automatically from either the onboarding context
(samAccountName, displayName, email, firstName, lastName, roleId, roleName, createdBy, runId)
or from a console prompt whose 'name' matches. @EmployeeNumber and @Shift come from the
two prompts defined in Roles/base-employee.json. A statement asking for a parameter that
nothing supplies fails loudly rather than silently inserting NULL.
_employeeNumberComment: Employee numbers are variable-length digit strings. If any of them can carry a
LEADING ZERO, the receiving SQL column must be a string type (VARCHAR/NVARCHAR),
not INT - an INT column silently turns 004821 into 4821, and the existsQuery that
makes re-runs safe would then stop matching.
_namingComment: Governs how every identifier is generated. Defined once here as the site standard;
an individual role file may override any part of it by including its own 'naming'
block, which merges over this one attribute by attribute.
format            The primary pattern. {token:N} takes the first N characters.
collisionFormats  Tried in order when the primary is taken. A format containing
{n} is retried with n = 2,3,4... {n} is never truncated.
transform         Applied in order. Put 'ascii' first so accents fold to letters
instead of being deleted by the filters that follow.
maxLength         Hard cap. 20 for sAMAccountName is an AD limit, not a preference.
validate          Regex the final value must match, or the candidate is rejected.
uniqueIn          Systems the value must be free in: 'ad', or 'sql:<SystemName>'
(which needs a 'uniqueQuery' on that system, below).

samAccountName._dotNote: TO USE dana.reyes STYLE USERNAMES, change three keys together: format -> "{firstName}.{lastName}", transform -> ["ascii", "keep:A-Za-z0-9.", "lower"], validate -> "^[a-z][a-z0-9.]{2,19}$", and update collisionFormats to match. The 'keep' transform is what preserves the dot; 'alphanumeric' would strip it straight back out. Run Test-OnboardingRole afterwards - it checks all three agree.

intranetUserId._note: Example of a system with a tighter convention: 7 characters, uppercase, letters and digits only.

password._modeNote: 'template' builds the password from the fields on the form. 'random' generates a cryptographically random string and ignores 'template'. 'length' applies to random mode only. To switch back, change mode to "random" - that one word is the whole change.
_securityWarning: A templated password is PREDICTABLE. Anyone who can work out the inputs can work out
the password, before the employee has logged in even once.
This matters more than usual with this particular template, because the employee
number is written into the AD 'description' attribute as 'Emp# ######', and that
attribute is readable by EVERY authenticated user in the domain. Initials come from
the display name, which is equally public. So any domain user can compute the initial
password of every pending new hire by reading the directory.
If you keep template mode, the mitigations that matter are:
- changePasswordAtLogon stays true in base-employee.json (it is)
- onboard close to the start date, so the window of exposure is short
- consider moving the employee number out of 'description' into a non-public
attribute, which removes the easy half of the guess
Switching mode to 'random' removes the issue entirely.
